resale_co.name: Certificate of Inspection / Continued Certificate of Occupancy (Certificate of Compliance under Chapter 90), resales or rentals
resale_co.issued_by: Chesterfield Township Construction Office (Code Enforcement Officer, acting as Township Housing Official)
resale_co.lead_time: The Township has 10 working days after a complete application to inspect; after all repairs and certifications are in, the certificate takes 3 business days to generate, so apply well before closing.
requirements: Physical inspection of the home; smoke and carbon monoxide detectors are tested by the Township inspector (or certification from the monitoring company if the system is monitored)
Working smoke detectors in each bedroom and smoke/carbon monoxide detectors on each floor; carbon monoxide detectors near the bedrooms
Original certifications (no copies or faxes) that the heater is operating correctly, for the heater chimney, for any wood burning fireplaces or woodstoves, and for their chimneys
Well water test by a certified testing agency if on well water; the buyer or tenant certifies they were told the results
GFI protection for outside outlets, outlets within 6 feet of the kitchen sink and bathroom/powder room outlets; three-prong outlet for the washer; no open spaces in the electrical panel
Guardrails and handrails on all stairways; halls and stairways lighted
Heater and water heater safety blow-off valve within 6 to 8 inches of the floor
Gutters, downspouts, second story window screens, broken windows, decks and porches in repair; no exposed exterior insulation
Large interior wall holes, missing tub and shower tiles and leaking faucets repaired; toilets working; no mold
No trash or rubbish on the property; house number visible on the front of the house or on the mailbox at the street

fees.label: Resale inspection, initial inspection plus one reinspection
fees.quote: After submitting the application and paying the $75 fee, requests for inspection may be made by calling the phone number listed above.

fees.label: Each additional inspection after the included reinspection
fees.quote: If additional inspections are required, there is a $50.00 fee per inspection.

resale_co.how_to_apply: Submit the online Application for Certificate of Inspection (linked from the Township's Certificate Of Inspection page and Forms list), choose the sale application type, and pay the $75 fee. Then call the Construction Office at 609-298-2311 (Code Enforcement ext. 140) to request the inspection; voice mail requests are accepted. Turn in original heater/chimney certifications and the well water form if needed. Fees are payable to the Township of Chesterfield.

resale_co.notes: Fees went up: Township Code 110-90 (amended November 14, 2024 by Ord. No. 2024-21) now sets $75 for the resale inspection plus one reinspection and $50 for each later inspection, and the Township's live Certificate Of Inspection page matches ($75 and $50.00). The old April 2024 paper form ($50 resale, $25 extra inspections) is gone; the application is now an online form at chesterfieldtwpnj.gov/media/5586 that asks for the closing date, buyer, bedrooms, water supply and accessory structures. Chapter 90 (Certificate of Compliance) requires the certificate before any sale, rental or new occupancy, allows a temporary certificate, and lets the buyer assume the seller's responsibility in writing. The Township site is behind a Cloudflare check, so pages were read through a text reader; the staff directory links email through a contact form only, so no email is recorded (an older page showed 'glenn [at] chesterfieldtwp.com'). The current Common Violations page no longer lists a fire extinguisher. Rentals use the same certificate and a separate registration.

requirements: Working smoke detectors in each bedroom and smoke/carbon monoxide detectors on each floor; carbon monoxide detectors in the vicinity of the bedrooms (tested by the Township inspector during the Certificate of Inspection)
Monitored systems: certification from the monitoring company that the system is operating correctly

fire_cert.notes: The NJ DCA is the fire code enforcing agency for Chesterfield (LEA registry code S; Fire Official Louis Kilmer, (609)633-6132), but the DCA state-towns list (revised 7/17/2026) does not mark Chesterfield 'SC' (state issues smoke certs), and the DCA directory lists 'Chesterfield Twp Constr Office' (300 Bordentown Chesterfield Rd, (609) 298-0426) for smoke detector compliance. The Township's Certificate Of Inspection page says its inspector tests smoke and CO detectors during the resale inspection, so the smoke/CO check is part of the Township certificate. The directory address and phone differ from the Township's (295 Bordentown-Chesterfield Rd., 609-298-2311). The current Township pages no longer mention a fire extinguisher, in line with P.L.2025, c.19.

other_items.label: Well water test
other_items.detail: If the home is on well water, the water must be tested by a certified testing agency and the buyer must certify they were told the results.

other_items.label: Heater and chimney certifications
other_items.detail: Original certifications that the heater is operating correctly, for the heater chimney, and for any wood burning fireplaces or woodstoves and their chimneys are required before the certificate is issued.

other_items.label: New owner notice
other_items.detail: Township Code 90 says the new owner must notify the Housing Official in writing of the change in ownership within 10 days after receiving the deed (this appears in the rental registration article).
